routes.description: Establish a likelihood comparison in which life-permitting fine-tuning is substantially more expected given classical perfect-being theism than given the complete admissible space of single-universe naturalistic alternatives.
routes.successCriteria: The route succeeds if it grounds the fine-tuning datum, supplies a defensible expectation of valuable conscious life under perfect-being theism, and shows that hypothesis augmentation, simulation, aggregated alternatives, and naturalistic parsimony do not erase the comparative evidential advantage.

motionBridge.description: Show that the posterior-confirming force of fine-tuning remains strong after the relevant theistic and naturalistic hypothesis spaces are compared.

centralBridges.description: Establish that life-permitting conditions are far less expected under single-universe naturalism than under a perfectly good creator with reasons to value conscious moral life.
Explain why admissible alien, simulation, time-travel, or fine-tuning-specific naturalistic alternatives do not collectively neutralize the likelihood asymmetry.
Justify an intrinsic-probability treatment under which the coherence or simplicity of perfect-being theism offsets the specificity of augmented naturalistic rivals.

subsidiaryBridges.description: Provide a principled basis for empirical evidence to discriminate between theism and broad naturalistic alternatives despite logical compatibility with multiple causes.
Account for naturalism's ontological economy and explain how it should be balanced against the claimed conditional-probability advantage.

routes.description: Undercut the strong-evidence inference by challenging the specification and aggregation of the rival hypothesis spaces, the predictive content of divine psychology, and the status of apparent fine-tuning as an objective datum.
routes.successCriteria: The route succeeds if theism cannot be assigned a sufficiently reliable likelihood advantage over the full naturalistic alternative space, or if uncertainty about priors, divine intentions, or the fine-tuning datum prevents the asserted strong confirmation.

motionBridge.description: Show that fine-tuning does not strongly discriminate in favor of God once hypothesis-space ambiguity and uncertain theistic predictions are included.

centralBridges.description: Require comparison with the aggregated space of admissible naturalistic explanations rather than with a selectively austere naturalistic hypothesis.
Establish that perfect goodness and other divine attributes do not yield sufficiently determinate predictions about creating life-permitting conditions.
Show that aggregation, modesty, coherence, and ontological parsimony leave the relevant intrinsic-probability comparison unresolved.

subsidiaryBridges.description: Demonstrate how apparently purposive or religious evidence can remain compatible with broad naturalistic agency explanations.
Test whether apparent fine-tuning is an objective feature requiring explanation or instead a sign that the operative physical theory is defective.

sections.title: The Fine-Tuning Datum and the Core Likelihood Comparison
sections.rationale: This section contains the motion's foundational issue: whether life-permitting parameters constitute an objective and improbable datum whose likelihood differs substantially between classical theism and single-universe naturalism.

sections.title: Naturalistic Alternatives and the Relevant Comparison Class
sections.rationale: The strength of the inference depends on whether theism must outperform one austere naturalistic hypothesis or the aggregated space of alien, simulation, time-travel, and other admissible naturalistic explanations.

sections.title: Divine Goodness, Agency, and Predictive Expectations
sections.rationale: A likelihood advantage for theism requires a defensible bridge from perfect divine goodness to the creation of valuable conscious life, while the opposing burden tests whether divine intentions remain too indeterminate.

sections.title: Intrinsic Probability, Coherence, Modesty, and Parsimony
sections.rationale: This issue determines how the prior plausibility of perfect-being theism compares with disjunctions of limited or augmented naturalistic hypotheses before the fine-tuning evidence is incorporated.

sections.title: Empirical Discrimination and Religious Ambiguity
sections.rationale: The parties dispute whether broad alternative explanations make empirical evidence persistently ambiguous and whether such ambiguity undercuts fine-tuning without foreclosing every possible non-empirical argument concerning God.
